items.name: RowSelection
items.summary: [`RowSelection`] represents selecting a subset of rows when scanning a parquet file.

methods.name: and_then
methods.summary: returns a [`RowSelection`] representing rows that are selected in both input [`RowSelection`]s.

methods.name: as_mask
methods.summary: Returns the underlying mask if this selection is mask-backed.

methods.name: from_consecutive_ranges
methods.signature: fn from_consecutive_ranges<I: Iterator<Item = Range<usize>>>(ranges: I, total_rows: usize) -> Self
methods.summary: Creates a [`RowSelection`] from an iterator of consecutive ranges to keep

methods.name: from_filters
methods.summary: Creates a [`RowSelection`] from a slice of [`BooleanArray`]

methods.name: from_iter
methods.signature: fn from_iter<T: IntoIterator<Item = RowSelection>>(iter: T) -> Self

methods.name: intersection
methods.summary: Compute the intersection of two [`RowSelection`] For example: self:      NNYYYYNNYYNYN other:     NYNNNNNNY

methods.name: iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over the [`RowSelector`]s for this [`RowSelection`].

methods.name: row_count
methods.summary: Returns the number of selected rows

methods.name: scan_ranges
methods.summary: Given an offset index, return the byte ranges for all data pages selected by `self`

methods.name: selects_any
methods.summary: Returns `true` if this [`RowSelection`] selects any rows

methods.name: skipped_row_count
methods.summary: Returns the number of de-selected rows

methods.name: split_off
methods.signature: fn split_off(&mut self, row_count: usize) -> Self
methods.summary: Splits off the first `row_count` from this [`RowSelection`]

methods.name: union
methods.summary: Compute the union of two [`RowSelection`] For example: self:      NNYYYYNNYYNYN other:     NYNNNNNNN
